October 27: In-Class Final Exam November 10: Final paper due on Canvas at midnight CST Assignments, Grading and Due Dates:

Students must read the assigned material before engaging in discussion and must contribute as much as possible to the in-class discussions. Each student is likely to find considerable benefit in the exchange of ideas, doubts, and criticisms during discussions. Much of the value of a graduate class is in the sharing of the knowledge and perspective that each participant brings to the sessions.
A final exam will be distributed during the final class session. The exam will cover all readings assigned for the class, as well as material discussed in class.

Students will prepare an analytical paper about an international topic of their choice. The paper will model an outstanding form of analytical writing as discussed in class. It will be 5-7 pages (double-spaced) and will examine and evaluate a contemporary international issue from a particular theoretical perspective and level of analysis. The final paper will be due on November 10 via Canvas.
This is a letter-graded course: A, B, C, D, or F. The standard grade scale will apply: 90%-100% = A; 80%-89% = B; 70%-79% = C; 60%-69% = D; below 60% = F.
